parsed.explanation: Combined regime: the national layer carries the heaviest exposure. Passport sex-marker restrictions are in effect after the November 2025 Supreme Court order, and entry screening refuses discrepant applicants and allows a possible lifetime fraud ineligibility finding. Immigration custody abuses are documented. The state adds a school and college facility designation duty covering private institutions, an August 2026 exact-match marker rule for licences, and school outing requirements. Mitigating: the state's facility law has no enforcement mechanism and no recorded case, marriage is recognised, courts have enjoined several measures, and 33 localities protect against gender-identity discrimination. The state does not criminalise visitors' presentation. Net: Elevated Risk, bounded by documented custody harm and entry-document exposure.

entry_documents.exposure: Passports now issued only M/F by sex at birth; foreign-ministry cable refuses cases with document discrepancy and allows a permanent fraud-ground ineligibility finding; passports confiscated or blocked, some travellers stranded. State Aug 2026 rule requires exact-matching birth certificate or passport for licence markers.
entry_documents.protection: Documented court challenge pending; fraud finding requires four elements and is not automatic; limited waivers exist.
entry_documents.interaction: Document mismatch at national entry is the trigger for refusal and possible investigation; state licence rules add domestic ID friction after entry.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Immigration custody: documented forced labour, beatings, solitary confinement and severe sexual abuse of trans men. Federal corrections policy imposes conversion-type treatment and stopped reporting trans prisoner numbers. One trespass arrest with 24-hour hold in another state's men's ward.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: Pretrial release was granted in the trespass case; no documented remedy working for custody abuse.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: A document or facility discrepancy can route a visitor into national custody, where birth-sex or sex-based placement and treatment harms are documented.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: Facility bans in government buildings across many states; this state's law covers K-12 and all colleges, public and private, requiring birth-certificate-based designation. Overnight accommodations included. No enforcement mechanism and no recorded case here.
federal_state_facilities.protection: Single-occupancy controlled-use rooms exempt; no state criminal penalty.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: Designation applies to institutions a visitor may enter (campuses, schools), so exposure is institutional refusal rather than police action.

care_services.exposure: Under-18 care ban status unresolved after 2025 re-injunction. National subpoenas of hospital records for under-19 patients and proposed rules barring public reimbursement for under-18 care. Adult-care rules were withdrawn and are not in force.
care_services.protection: Adult care not restricted by documented rules in force; the care ban is currently enjoined by an appeals court per the dossier.
care_services.interaction: A visitor who needs care can be exposed through hospital records being subpoenaed nationally.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: National counterterrorism strategy names 'radically pro-transgender' groups as targets; reward system for leadership identification. State school law requires staff to out LGBTQ students to parents. Candidate disqualification for non-disclosure of birth name.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: Counterterrorism statement disclaims targeting people who merely disagree; several executive orders are enjoined.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Official framing can translate into enforcement attention; outing duties extend this exposure to minors.

minors_guardians.exposure: School facility designation applies to students and visitor-accompanying minors at covered institutions. Staff must out LGBTQ students to parents. Federal directive to prosecute teachers facilitating social transition. Under-18 care ban uncertain. Travelling minor with trans parent faces document checks.
minors_guardians.protection: Parental opt-out for some curriculum; no state criminal penalty for facilities.
minors_guardians.interaction: A minor's documents and school designation can disclose a parent's or child's status to officials and schools.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: No visitor-specific street violence documented in the dossier. National hate-crime statute covers gender identity; only 23 states have bias statutes covering gender identity.
street_violence_police_response.protection: National hate-crime statute; 33 local ordinances; state executive-order employment protection.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Protection depends on local enforcement, which the dossier does not document for visitors.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: Multiple national measures are unresolved in court. Enforcement practice of school facility law, county refusals on birth-certificate corrections, and August 2026 licence rule text are unknown.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Courts have enjoined several orders; birth-certificate corrections permitted since 2021 in most counties; marriage recognised.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Uncertain measures in effect at time of travel shift exposure unpredictably; checking current status is required.

anchor_checks.comparison: 0.35-A has a universal visitor register with discretionary exclusion and no effective appeal. This dossier has entry refusal for document discrepancy and a possible permanent fraud finding, but no universal register and some working court relief. It is similar in exclusion risk and somewhat higher on remedy availability, so the score sits near 0.35.

0.25-C has birth-sex custody housing with reported assaults and cross-dressing arrests in administrative buildings. This dossier documents comparable custody harms and birth-sex facility rules, but the state's own facility law has no enforcement, and no visitor arrest is recorded here. Slightly higher than 0.25-C.

0.45-A has biometric linking, lengthy detentions and penalties for deceptive presentation, with narrow anti-discrimination recourse. This dossier shares the document-discrepancy exposure but has no documented penalty for presentation and more active court checks. Slightly lower than 0.45-A on the state layer, and comparable or worse on national custody abuse, so placed at roughly 0.33.

parsed.synthesis: The national document regime and entry screening create the main universal exposure: visitors with mismatched documents can be refused, held or referred for a fraud finding, and national custody has documented sexual abuse and forced treatment. The state layer adds a school and college facility duty and outing mandates, but these carry no criminal penalty or documented enforcement, and marriage recognition plus local ordinances give some protection. Court injunctions on several measures mean the operative position must be verified at travel. Overall the regime is Elevated Risk, lifted slightly by the state's lack of criminal enforcement but held down by national custody harms.
